title: Acceptors-fairness-splay-annotated-retro
body:
Executive summary:

On 2029-03-02 at ~09:12 UTC, hosted-api began exhibiting elevated p95/p99 streaming tail latency and a small but rapidly growing wave of 5xx errors for active streaming sessions. The impact peaked between 09:17–09:36 UTC with ~18% of streaming sessions experiencing dropped fragments or stalls (clients observed reconnects and partial payloads). Traffic throttles and automatic hedging amplified load on acceptor queues, causing a cascading fairness imbalance that amplified head-of-line blocking in acceptor threads.

Customer impact:
- Duration: ~24 minutes of degraded streaming quality with periodic reconnections, followed by several hours of elevated retry rates.
- Scope: ~3.2k active streaming sessions affected across a single region (us-west2). No data loss of persisted outputs; some user-visible partial responses and increased TTFB.
- Severity: P0 (streaming degradation producing customer-visible failures and elevated error budgets).

What changed recently:
- On 2029-02-28 we rolled out a fairness heuristic (PR #3112) to the acceptor scheduler aimed at reducing starvation for long-poll connections by preferentially rotating session tokens across connection age buckets. The heuristic was enabled in us-west2 via a config flip at 08:45 UTC on 2029-03-02 as part of routine rollout.
- There was a lower-than-usual KV-cache hit rate starting 09:10 UTC due to an ongoing metadata compaction job; combined with client-side bursting from a large gaming partner (identified in telemetry) this produced unusual sequence-length and prefix distributions.

Timeline (concise):
- 08:45 UTC: Fairness heuristic enabled (canary -> region).
- 09:10 UTC: KV metadata compaction begins; cache hit-rate drops ~12 percentage points.
- 09:12 UTC: Alert: streaming p95 and 5xx rate begins to climb (SRE pager).
- 09:15 UTC: Oncall begins triage; initial hypothesis: client burst or upstream load generator.
- 09:17 UTC: Observed acceptor queue depth growing and acceptor latency skewed heavily to a subset of threads.
- 09:20 UTC: Hedge amplification observed — retries/hedges targeting slow sessions increased concurrency on acceptors.
- 09:22 UTC: Traffic routing to dedicated fallback triggered for a subset of tenants; partial mitigation for non-streaming paths.
- 09:25 UTC: Emergency rollback of fairness heuristic in us-west2 config; immediate reduction in acceptor skew.
- 09:30 UTC: 5xx spike subsided; streaming stalls reduced, but elevated retry churn persisted until 11:00 UTC.
- 11:05 UTC: Post-incident telemetry and tracing collection completed.

Root cause (summary):
The acceptor fairness heuristic interacted poorly with a transient change in workload (client bursts + lower KV-cache hits). The heuristic was designed to rotate tokens by connection-age buckets; under the observed distribution it scheduled many long-lived sessions onto a small subset of acceptor threads while short, high-throughput sessions kept being requeued. This created head-of-line blocking: expensive sessions held acceptor thread CPU and I/O long enough that hedged followups and scheduler timeouts increased concurrency and q-length on remaining threads, producing cascading stalls and an increase in internal 5xx from upstream timeouts.

Contributing factors:
- Rollout timing: region enable at 08:45 UTC without extended traffic canary.
- Heuristic assumptions: expected uniform session distribution; real traffic had a heavy tail of long-lived streaming sessions from a partner.
- KV-cache compaction reducing cache-hit-rate temporarily, increasing average tokenization and prefix-processing CPU per request.
- Circuit breaker cooldowns and hedging thresholds tuned aggressively for latency SLOs, which increased retry-driven amplification during the failure window.
- Observability gaps: no per-acceptor-thread heatmap on the primary SRE dashboard; detection relied on bespoke traces and oncall sleuthing.

Detection and diagnosis notes:
- Primary signals: sustained p95/p99 rise for streaming session durations, acceptor queue_depth metric rising > 800 for thread pool, and a correlating spike in hedged request_rate.
- Useful queries: 1) acceptor.thread_queue_length{region=us-west2} by thread_id; 2) streaming.session_reconnect_rate{region=us-west2}; 3) kv_cache.hit_rate{region=us-west2} over 30m window.
- Traces: sampled traces showed repeated requeues of the same session ids across acceptor threads; traces included stack frames hitting tokenizer and cache-miss paths.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- 09:25 UTC: Rolled back the region config enabling the fairness heuristic (fast rollback via feature-flag).
- 09:28 UTC: Increased acceptor thread pool headroom by +20% (temporary), which reduced queue pressure while rollback propagated.
- 09:30 UTC: Adjusted circuit-breaker cooldown on hedging to add a 300ms backoff window to avoid immediate duplicate hedges against slow sessions.
- 09:45 UTC: Disabled scheduled metadata compaction (until safe window) to allow KV cache to warm back.

Why the rollback helped:
Removing the rotation heuristic returned scheduling to the prior default, which distributed work more evenly across acceptor threads for this workload. That eliminated the pathological concentration of expensive sessions on a subset of threads, breaking the head-of-line cascade.

Longer-term remediation and action items (owner + ETA):
- FIX-1: Add per-acceptor-thread heatmap and alert (SRE-dashboard-heatmap) to detect thread skew in <2min. Owner: Arjun Patel. ETA: 2029-03-16.
- FIX-2: Add rollout-gate: traffic-based canary (route 1% traffic for 30m) for acceptor scheduler heuristic toggles. Owner: Lina Gomez. ETA: 2029-03-09.
- FIX-3: Rework fairness heuristic to include cost-estimation (estimated CPU + io per session) so rotation weights consider per-session cost, not just age. Owner: Serving Runtime team (Samir Rao). ETA: 2029-04-01.
- FIX-4: Soften hedging thresholds under acceptor-queue-pressure signal (automatic hedging suppression) to avoid amplification loops. Owner: eng-sre + serving-runtime. ETA: 2029-03-23.
- FIX-5: Add KV-cache compaction safety check: pause compaction if cache_hit_rate < 80% or streaming sessions > threshold. Owner: infra-storage. ETA: 2029-03-22.
- FIX-6: Document runbook steps for acceptor skew incidents (new playbook section) and run a tabletop drill. Owner: Maya Chen. ETA: 2029-03-12.

Runbook draft excerpt (for future oncall):
- Symptoms to watch: rising acceptor.thread_queue_length in a subset of threads; p95 streaming latency increasing while p50 stable; hedged_request_rate rising > 2x baseline.
- Fast triage: run acceptor_thread_heatmap and identify top-3 offending thread_ids. If one thread has >40% of pending work, escalate.
- Immediate short-term actions: 1) flip scheduler fairness feature-flag off for affected region; 2) increase acceptor pool headroom by 15–30%; 3) if hedging_rate > 1.5x baseline, increase hedging cooldown by +200–500ms.
- When to rollback: if error-rate > 5% or sustained p99 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes after mitigation attempts.

Telemetry & dashboards to add:
- Per-thread heatmap for acceptor pools (by region + host) with alert when top-3 threads > 50% of queue.
- Hedging amplification waveform: hedged_request_rate / initial_request_rate over 1m sliding windows.
- KV-cache compaction guard metric / warning.

Post-incident notes and learnings:
- Feature flag rollouts that touch scheduling semantics need a traffic-driven canary and a short dry-run period where heatmaps/telemetry are explicitly monitored.
- Heuristics that assume workload stationarity can be disastrous in the presence of temporary cache degradation or client bursts — incorporate cost-aware scheduling.
- Hedging and circuit-breaker policies should be adaptive to observed queue pressure to prevent retry amplification.

Communications and follow-ups:
- CS / Customer comms: outage summary and remediation timeline drafted (CS draft id: CS-7981).
- Exec summary: one-paragraph summary to be shared with CTO and Head of Product by 2029-03-06. Owner: Maya Chen.
- Postmortem review: schedule blameless review with SRE + Serving Runtime + Infra on 2029-03-09. Owner: Lina Gomez.

Appendix (diagnostic snippets):
- Quick PromQLs used during triage:
  * topk(10, sum by (thread_id) (acceptor_thread_queue_length{region="us-west2"}))
  * rate(hedged_requests_total[1m]) / rate(requests_total[1m])
  * kv_cache_hit_rate{region="us-west2"}

- Representative trace id showing requeue loop: trace: 8f7a2c9b.... (stored in tracing service, tag: acceptor-splay-2029-03-02).

Draft status and next steps:
This doc is a draft intended for SRE review. Please add comments inline or on the Linear issue INFR-482. After review, the final postmortem will be published to Confluence and the runbook will be appended to the hosted-api incident playbooks.

Oncall notes (raw):
- 09:13: weird cadence — p50 ok, p99 climbing; started paging.
- 09:18: acceptor_queue heatmap shows thread ids 12, 19 with 65% of pending work.
- 09:24: toggled feature-flag rollback; small improvement by 09:27.
- 09:40: hedging still noisy; applied cooldown bump.
- 10:10: traffic stabilized but retry churn persisted; left mitigations in place and monitored.

Owners contact list:
- Maya Chen (SRE lead) — maya@redwood.ai
- Arjun Patel (SRE) — arjun@redwood.ai
- Samir Rao (Serving Runtime) — samir@redwood.ai
- Lina Gomez (Release Eng) — lina@redwood.ai

End of draft.
